messages:
Priya: PagerDuty fired for customer BlueFjord (vpc-821). Possible cross-tenant routing observed. paging p1? :rotating_light:
PagerDuty Bot: Incident created: P1 - vpc-821 potential tenant isolation breach (incident#1876543210). Escalation: on-call SRE team.
Jamal: I'm on it, checking routing tables for the dedicated pool attached to vpc-821. Starting packet capture on the egress nodes.
Lina (SRE): Thx. Quick ask — is BlueFjord on dedicated-pool-5 or a shared-dedicated mix? I remember a custom routing rule last quarter.
Evgeny (eng-runtime): They were moved to dedicated-pool-5 in Nov, but there was a temporary share window during scale up. Pulling allocation history..
Marco (CS): BlueFjord reports a few customer requests returning data they don't recognize. They're very worried. I've told them we're triaging and will provide an ETA.
Jamal: Found an odd iptables rule on node gpu-57: `-A FORWARD -s 10.8.0.0/24 -d 10.9.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT` — should not be there for dedicated pools. Dumping iptables and routing table to /tmp/1876543210/
Jamal: routing table snippet:
```
10.8.0.0/24 via 172.16.100.2 dev eth1
10.9.1.0/24 via 172.16.100.3 dev eth2
default via 172.16.100.1
```
Lina (SRE): That FORWARD rule could explain path bleed. Did someone apply a transient route for testing?
Evgeny (eng-runtime): I see a recent rollout that touched pool routing policies at 02:12 UTC — correlating. Fetching rollout metadata now.
AuditBot: Route-policy-change detected by config-audit at 2026-03-15T02:12:14Z. Author: infra-ci-bot. Change-id: rpol-9b3f.
Priya: Who approved rpol-9b3f? That sounds like the kernel patch we rolled last week. If infra-ci-bot did it, maybe mis-template.
Jamal: For immediate mitigation, I'd like to remove the FORWARD accept, reload conntrack, and relinker routes to enforce tenant isolation. Propose commands:
```
iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.8.0.0/24 -d 10.9.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT
sudo systemctl restart netfilter-persistent
conntrack -D --orig-src 10.8.0.0/24
```
Lina (SRE): +1 to remove rule, but hold on conntrack flush until we confirm impact window with CS. Marco, possible downtime?
Marco (CS): BlueFjord says they can tolerate a brief pause (under 2 minutes) for mitigation if it prevents exposure. Give me a 90s heads up before conntrack flush.
Evgeny (eng-runtime): Pushing a targeted rollback of rpol-9b3f to just dedicated-pool-5. This will re-apply the strict next-hop policies. Rolling patch to 1 node for canary first (gpu-57).
Jamal: Can confirm GPU-57 now has the FORWARD rule removed. Monitoring flows. Starting tcpdump filter: `tcpdump -i eth1 host 10.8.0.23 or host 10.9.1.42 -w /tmp/1876543210/trace.pcap`
Jamal: Early look: a handful of 10.9.1.* flows originating towards 10.8.0.* at 02:09:xx, likely short-lived. Extracting HTTP headers.
Priya: Collect logs for model serving process on those nodes too (inference logs + kv-cache access). We need to prove no actual model artifact leaked — mostly headers/paths seen but confirm payloads.
Evgeny (eng-runtime): Can we snapshot KV-cache boundaries? I requested kv-mgr dump for partition ids used by BlueFjord and adjacent tenant. ETA ~2m.
AuditBot: KV-dump job queued: job-4827.
Lina (SRE): After canary rollback on gpu-57, flows stopped. Rolling to rest of pool-5 now. Will stage during 30s window per node.
Priya: Marco, please let BlueFjord know we removed the suspect rule and are rolling the fix. We'll share pcap and header summary once validated.
Marco (CS): Sending a short update now. They asked for CISO contact — cc'ing me and I'll loop.
Jamal: Uploaded pcap + extracted HTTP headers to secure bucket s3://redwood-incident-evidence/1876543210. Included mapping of conntrack entries and PID->process mapping.
Priya: Evidence checklist: pcap, routing table before/after, iptables diff, kv-cache dump, model-serving logs, change-id rpol-9b3f. Make sure all filenames are timestamped.
Evgeny (eng-runtime): kv-mgr returned boundaries. No overlapping partition ids found between ft-BlueFjord and ft-NeighborTenant. So KV boundary intact. Looks like routing rule caused forwarding only for some ephemeral flows (control plane misroute).
Lina (SRE): Confirming: no model payloads in pcaps. Only metadata-level headers and a few keepalive probes. Good.
Marco (CS): Relaying to BlueFjord: we found a misapplied route policy by infra-ci-bot; we've removed it and stopped cross-tenant forwarding. No model payloads observed. Customer relieved for now, requests final postmortem and proof artifacts.
Priya: Assigning follow-up tasks:
- Evgeny: root-cause analysis of infra-ci templating that allowed rpol-9b3f to target dedicated pool (ETA 4h)
- Jamal: collect full node forensic tarball for gpu-57..gpu-60 (ETA 2h)
- Lina: prepare mitigation playbook addition for automated route-policy verification in canaries (ETA 24h)
- Marco: coordinate with BlueFjord CISO for evidence handoff and sign NDAs if needed (ETA 1h)
PagerDuty Bot: Incident 1876543210 status: Mitigated -> Acknowledged -> Monitoring.
Priya: Handoff to next on-call in 30m: Lina will take lead, Jamal you can go OOO after forensic samples uploaded. Keep channel pinned.
Lina (SRE): Taking lead. I'll summarize a tl;dr and create postmortem draft in #postmortems and attach evidence.
Evgeny (eng-runtime): Noted. I'll include config diff and CI templating logs.
Marco (CS): BlueFjord asked for a 24h SLA on final report. I'll push the ask, but we should be conservative.
Priya: Thanks everyone. Closing thread for live mitigation — leave comments here for any late artefacts.
